title: Claude Sonnet 5.5 on iac-bench 2026-10
summary: How Claude Sonnet 5.5 did on iac-bench 2026-10: an overall composite of 86.1, scores per fixture, strengths, weaknesses and the patterns in its OpenTofu modules.
body_markdown:
Developer Anthropic


API identifier` claude-sonnet-5-5`


Access Anthropic API


Weights Closed


List price (USD / M tokens, in / out) 2.00 / 10.00 (OpenRouter, 2026-10-23)


Evaluated 2026-10-22 (generation) · 2026-10-23 (judge)

**Overall composite** **86.1** (95% CI 84.8–88.2)

Mechanical only / judge only 82.5 (rank 4) / 94.7 (rank 3)

## Summary


Claude Sonnet 5.5 is in the top group overall. Its Cloud SQL result (G002) is second only to GPT-6 Astra's, by under one point. It is the cheapest model in that group, at roughly a tenth of the per-attempt cost of Claude Fable 5.1. All 9 attempts planned.


Its two security findings come from a single omission on App Service: in 2 of 3 attempts it never sets the two basic-auth publishing flags, which the Azure provider enables by default. The same blocks set HTTPS-only, TLS 1.2 and FTPS-off correctly.

Definitions are in[Scoring criteria](https://www.massdriver.cloud/blogs/iac-bench-2026-10-scoring-criteria) .


## Strengths


- **Locked posture on Cloud SQL (3/3).** It sets private IP only and` ENCRYPTED_ONLY` , and merges consumer flags *under* a fixed map:` merge(var.database_flags, local.enforced_flags)` . The judge cited this merge order for *Anti-patterns* 2 in every attempt.
- **Identity-first access.** Cloud SQL users are IAM-only, with conditioned` cloudsql.instanceUser` grants (E3, E5, E6 and E7 in 3/3), so no password variable exists. *Sensitive values* scored 2 in 9/9 attempts. App Service pulls images with a managed identity (E4, 3/3).
- **S3 hygiene.** In every attempt:


- bucket-owner-enforced ownership;
- cleanup of incomplete multipart uploads;
- a TLS-only bucket policy;
- the regional domain output;
- ready-made consumer IAM policies.


- **Cross-input preconditions:** S3 transitions must come before expiry; Cloud SQL edition must be compatible with tier; App Service scale-in must stay below scale-out.


## Weaknesses


- **App Service H2 (security finding, 2/3).**` ftp_publish_basic_authentication_enabled` and` webdeploy_publish_basic_authentication_enabled` are absent on the app and the slot, so both stay at the provider default (on). The attempt that sets them instead takes` minimum_tls_version` as an input, which loses` H3` .
- **Provider pinning.**


- ` B1` lost in 6/9 attempts, including unbounded` >=` on S3.
- No` provider "aws"` block on S3 in 3/3 attempts (` H15` ).


- **Cloud SQL drops databases removed from the input** (` H11` , 3/3). Backups and point-in-time recovery cannot be turned off.
- **S3 access logging that cannot deliver** (` H13` , 3/3).


## Characteristic patterns


- **The same four files every time:**` main.tf` ,` variables.tf` ,` outputs.tf` and` versions.tf` , in 8/9 attempts. The judge gave *File layout* 1 in 5/9 for a 200–400-line` main.tf` .
- **Input counts sit just at each fixture's budget ceiling,** not well under it.
- **Plenty of validation, unevenly precise.** For example, a` sku_name` pattern that rejects valid SKUs such as P0v3, in 3/3 App Service attempts.


## Representative excerpt


` G003/claude-sonnet-5-5-e1/main.tf` lines 119–133


```text
service_plan_id         = azurerm_service_plan.this.id
https_only              = true
client_affinity_enabled = false
app_settings            = local.app_settings
tags                    = local.tags


identity {
type = "SystemAssigned"
}


site_config {
always_on                               = true
http2_enabled                           = true
ftps_state                              = "Disabled"
minimum_tls_version                     = "1.2"


```


HTTPS, FTPS-off and TLS 1.2 are hardcoded, but neither basic-auth publishing flag is set. Both stay at the provider default (on). This is the cause of the` H2` finding.


## Notes on the judge


The judge gave the two App Service attempts with the security finding *Anti-patterns* 2, citing their hardcoded HTTPS and TLS settings. The judge reads source, and a provider default that the source never mentions does not appear in it. The rubric's plan-based check is what catches this class of defect.
